 Job Scan Home / CST & VAT / Cement Unit Cannot Be Denied Thrust Sector Status for Involving in Grinding or Mixing Activities: Orissa HC Directs Reconsideration of VAT Reimbursement Claim [Read Order] CST & VAT Law Report Cement Unit Cannot Be Denied Thrust Sector Status for Involving in Grinding or Mixing Activities: Orissa HC Directs Reconsideration of VAT Reimbursement Claim [Read Order]
 VAT reimbursement to be considered Thrust Sector status rejected solely because unit existed before IPR 2007
 By  Kalyani B. Nair · 5 Nov 2026, 9:55 pm IST 3′ read Save Get the day's tax rulings in your inbox 
 Email address Subscribe × The Orissa High Court directed reconsideration of a cement unit’s Thrust Sector status and Value Added Tax (VAT) reimbursement claim, holding that eligibility cannot be denied merely because its manufacturing process involves grinding or mixing.
 The petitioner acquired M/s. IDCOL Cement Ltd. in 2003 and merged it with its existing unit, Bargarh Cement Works, in 2005. Under the Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 2007, existing units undertaking expansion were eligible for VAT reimbursement. The petitioner claimed to have invested Rs. 585.57 crores from March 2007 to December 2010, increasing the unit’s capacity from 0.96 million to 2.5 million tonnes per annum, with commercial production commencing on 01.01.2011.
 In 2011, the petitioner sought recognition as a Thrust Sector industry and VAT reimbursement. The District Industries Centre (DIC) verified its investment, employment and eligibility and forwarded the claim to the concerned authorities. VAT payments of Rs. 50.75 crores for FY 2011-12 were also certified, but no final sanction was issued.
